title: Difference Quotient of a Cubic
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x)=x^3, expand (x+h)^3 and simplify the difference quotient (f(x+h)-f(x))/h, h != 0.

steps.title: Expand the Cube
steps.explanation: Apply the binomial formula to the incremented input.
steps.why: The cubic expansion is the standard trinomial-plus-h^3 identity.

steps.title: Subtract f(x)
steps.explanation: The x^3 terms cancel, leaving only powers of h in the numerator.
steps.why: Subtracting the original value isolates the change produced by h.

steps.title: Factor and Divide by h
steps.explanation: Every remaining term contains h, so factoring it out and cancelling with the denominator finishes the simplification.
steps.why: h != 0 allows the cancellation, leaving a polynomial in x and h.
